processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification; liquid metal poured into a copper mold
processing_steps.heating_or_cooling_rate: calculated maximum cooling rate ~5 x 10^3 K/s
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingot made from high purity Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.9%), Al (99.9%), C (99.8%) and Cr (99.9%), reheated to melt by an induction coil; 0Cr strip contained no Cr addition. Obtained strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm.

processing_steps.method: annealing in a vacuum electric resistance furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Annealing treatment applied to the near-rapidly solidified 0Cr strip; promotes precipitation of κ-carbides in the Cr-free strip.

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase austenite (γ, major matrix) + ferrite (δ) microstructure; after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h the Cr-free (0Cr) strip still consists of austenite and ferrite, κ-carbides precipitate in the austenite matrix (κ(111) peak at ~41.4° unique to the 0Cr trace), and DO3-ordered nano-domains appear in the ferrite.

phases_present.crystal_structure: FCC (XRD; austenite lattice constant of 0Cr strip reported as 3.70 Å)

phases_present.morphology: fine precipitates in the austenite matrix (clear {100}-type superlattice in SADP)

microstructure_list.region: δ-ferrite particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

phases_present.volume_fraction: ~10.2 vol% (as-cast value; ferrite size and fraction of annealed strips almost remain the same)
phases_present.morphology: rod-like to short-elongated δ-ferrite particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

phases_present.crystal_structure: ordered bcc (DO3 superlattice reflections, (hkl) all odd or all even)

defect_interactions.interaction_type: slip band formation and dislocation activity during tensile deformation
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After tensile fracture the average slip-band spacing of annealed 0Cr increases to ~190 nm and the average slip-band width is 20.5 nm; finer slip bands with smaller spacing and low dislocation density are associated with high ductility, and both slip bands and dislocations contribute to ductility of this austenitic low-density steel.

interfaces.slip_behavior: In annealed 0Cr, more κ-carbides (average diameter 14 nm) act as barriers to dislocations (dislocations can only pass through κ-carbides with diameter < 10 nm), leading to shear localization and fewer slip bands, so total elongation decreases; average slip-band spacing after fracture increases from ~90 nm (as-cast) to ~190 nm (annealed).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Annealing at 550 °C for 5 h promotes precipitation of κ-carbides in the Cr-free austenite (κ(111) at ~41.4°) and induces DO3 ordering in the ferrite, while reducing dislocation density; the austenite + ferrite assemblage is unchanged.
interfaces.interface_notes: In the 0Cr strip κ-carbides are visible at the austenite/ferrite phase boundary; the {100}-type κ superlattice is present in the austenite SADP after annealing.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests on MTS Criterion Model 44 with 10 kN capacity; each value averaged over 3 measurements

stress_strain_curves.value: Engineering stress-strain curve of annealed 0Cr stays almost flat just below the 900 MPa line and ends with a vertical drop between 20 and 30% strain (Fig. 8a); true stress-strain and strain hardening rate curves in Fig. 8b.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: increment of yield strength after annealing: +158 MPa; increment of total elongation after annealing: −10.7 % (annealed 0Cr vs as-cast 0Cr)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/Max-2200, Cu target, operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, scan rate 4° per min
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases of strips after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 0Cr shows γ + δ reflections plus a κ(111) peak at ~41.4° indicating κ-carbide precipitation; austenite lattice constant 3.70 Å for 0Cr.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM, BF/DF) with selected-area diffraction (SADP)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF/DF imaging; scale bars 500 nm (200 nm for DF of 0Cr κ-carbides)
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine austenite and ferrite microstructure, κ-carbide/DO3 precipitation, dislocations of annealed strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 0Cr austenite shows clear κ-carbide superlattice ([001]γ+[001]κ) with increased intensity and dense speckled κ-carbides (average diameter 14 nm); DO3 superlattice present in ferrite; dislocation density reduced after annealing but still lowest for the 0Cr strip.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MTS Criterion Model 44 mechanical property tester with 10 kN capacity
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: strain rate 1 x 10^-3 s^-1; gauge size 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm; >3 specimens per test
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure tensile properties (YS, UTS, TE) of as-cast and annealed strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 0Cr: YS 882 ± 6 MPa, UTS 934 ± 4 MPa, TE 30.1 ± 2 %.
0Cr strip measured composition (wt.%): Fe Bal., Mn 26.6, Al 9.1, C 1.2, Cr – (no Cr).

characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize microstructure of strips after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 0Cr shows a fully dendritic/cellular surface with clearly observable grain boundaries and dendritic structure.

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the 0Cr strip (ICP, Table 1): Fe Bal., Mn 26.6, Al 9.1, C 1.2 wt.%, Cr '–' (no Cr added); measured average density 6.49 g/cm3.
Increment of yield strength of the 0Cr strip after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h is +158 MPa; increment of total elongation after annealing is −10.7 % (annealed vs as-cast, Table 2/Fig. 4).
XRD (by JADE) austenite lattice constant of the 0Cr strip is 3.70 Å (reported with the as-cast strips).
Average diameter of κ-carbides is 14 nm in the annealed 0Cr strip, versus 8 nm in the as-cast 0Cr strip; dislocations can only pass through κ-carbides with diameter < 10 nm.
Average slip-band spacing in the annealed 0Cr strip after tensile fracture is ~190 nm, and the average slip-band width is 20.5 nm (as-cast 0Cr spacing ~90 nm, width 13.4 nm).

Unlike the Cr-containing strips, the annealed Cr-free (0Cr) strip shows a clear κ(111) diffraction peak at ~41.4°, confirming that annealing at 550 °C for 5 h promotes κ-carbide precipitation in the Cr-free strip; this peak is absent in the 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr annealed strips.
Ferrite fraction of the 0Cr strip is 10.2 vol% (as-cast quantitative measurement); the size and fraction of ferrite in annealed strips almost remain the same.
After annealing, DO3 superlattice reflections (and thus δ+DO3 ordered ferrite domains) appear in all strips including 0Cr and 3Cr, indicating DO3 ordering induced by the 550 °C/5 h anneal.

As-cast 0Cr strip average strain hardening rate in the steady hardening stage is 1626 MPa (for reference; the annealed-strip strain hardening rate of 0Cr is not given numerically, only that it decreases relative to as-cast except for 9Cr).
